front: Breadth and depth of agile approaches
back: Breadth: how much of the life cycle is covered. Depth: how prescriptive the guidance is.
A lightweight framework that helps people, teams and organizations generate value through adaptive solutions for complex problems.
Empiricism (knowledge from experience and observation) and lean thinking (reduce waste, focus on essentials).
Transparency, inspection, adaptation.
Commitment, focus, openness, respect, courage.
One Product Owner, one Scrum Master, Developers; typically 10 or fewer; cross-functional and self-managing.
Accountable for maximizing product value and for Product Backlog management. One person, not a committee.
Accountable for establishing Scrum and the team's effectiveness; coaches, causes impediments to be removed.
Create the Sprint Backlog plan, build to the Definition of Done, adapt the plan daily, hold each other accountable.
Sprint: one month or less. Planning 8 h, Daily Scrum 15 min, Review 4 h, Retrospective 3 h.
Only the Product Owner, when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
Product Backlog: Product Goal. Sprint Backlog: Sprint Goal. Increment: Definition of Done.

front: Item not meeting the Definition of Done
back: Cannot be released or presented at the Sprint Review; returns to the Product Backlog.

front: Is the Sprint Review a release gate?
back: No. An Increment may be delivered to stakeholders before the end of the Sprint.
Communication, simplicity, feedback, courage, respect.
Pair programming, test-first programming, continuous integration, 10-minute build, refactoring, user stories, sustainable pace.
Start where you are; no prescribed timeboxes; pull work; limit WIP; finishing beats starting.
Visualize the workflow, limit WIP, manage flow, make policies explicit, implement feedback loops, improve collaboratively.
A family of methods whose rigor grows with team size and criticality; osmotic communication, frequent delivery.
Constraint-driven: cost, quality and time fixed at the outset; scope prioritized to meet them.
Model, features list, plan by feature, design by feature, build by feature; for large software projects.
Ideas as hypotheses: build a minimum viable product, then build, measure, learn; persevere or pivot.
Representatives of several teams of three to nine meet, typically two to three times a week, to coordinate and remove impediments.
SAFe: portfolio, program, team levels around value streams. LeSS: single-team Scrum kept as far as possible. Scrum@Scale: minimum viable governance.
Only when single-team agile works. Otherwise remove the organizational impediments first; start small.
